prompt: Create a phased plan for extracting notification delivery from a monolith into an independently deployable service while preserving existing transactional email behavior. Map callers/data ownership, decide transitional contracts, sequence dual-read/write or outbox changes where justified, include shadowing/reconciliation, capacity/operability/security dependencies, rollback at each phase, and define what evidence would allow cutover. Do not turn the plan into speculative microservice code.

requirements: architecture packet listing monolith callers, notification tables, queue, and deployment constraints
behavioral compatibility requirements for existing notification types
operability and data-migration constraints including rollback after partial cutover
plan rubric requiring dependency graph, phase gates, owners, and verification evidence
paired same-model skill/no-skill execution from the identical starting snapshot

evidence: Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification
hierarchy boundary and specialist selection rationale
source/version boundary when facts can drift

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual planning boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (children=architecture-planning,business-case-analysis,migration-planning,product-management,project-program-management,release-planning,startup-operations; near-neighbor=accessibility-practice), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Translate the task contract into coherent dependency-ordered work with explicit acceptance criteria, risks, and verification.
Extraction sequencing preserves one authoritative owner at each phase and supplies reconciliation/rollback evidence so transitional duplication cannot become ambiguous production truth.
The result must not treat a happy path, generated artifact, compilation, or unsupported assumption as sufficient proof of planning correctness.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (Acceptance criteria; Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale; Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
